# Layout

A validated allocation request: a size, and the alignment its address must satisfy.

```rux
pub struct Layout {
    pub size: uint;
    pub alignment: uint;
}
```

Copy and owns nothing. Every instance is valid, because [`New`](/docs/api/allocator/layout#new) refuses to build an invalid one: the alignment is a
power of two, and the size rounded up to that alignment does not pass the end of the address space.
A size of zero is valid and is not an allocation of nothing — see `Allocate` for what an allocator does with it.

## Fields

| Name        | Type   | Description                                                             |
| ----------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size`      | `uint` | The number of bytes asked for, before any rounding.                     |
| `alignment` | `uint` | The alignment the address must be a multiple of. Always a power of two. |

## Associated functions

<h3 id="for-value"><code>ForValue</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ForValue<T>() -> Layout
```

A layout for one value of `T`, using its actual size and alignment.
No value is copied or consumed. Cannot fail, runs in constant time, and allocates nothing.

| Type parameter | Description          |
| -------------- | -------------------- |
| `T`            | the type to describe |

**Returns**: `T`'s own size and alignment

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Layout.rux#L31)

<h3 id="for-array"><code>ForArray</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ForArray<T>(count: uint) -> Layout?
```

A layout for `count` consecutive values of `T`, or absent when the size would overflow.
No value is copied or consumed. A zero count describes empty storage at `T`'s alignment.
Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

| Type parameter | Description      |
| -------------- | ---------------- |
| `T`            | the element type |

| Name    | Type   | Description       |
| ------- | ------ | ----------------- |
| `count` | `uint` | how many elements |

**Returns**: the array layout, or `none` if its size cannot be represented

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Layout.rux#L42)

<h3 id="new"><code>New</code></h3>

```rux
pub func New(size: uint, alignment: uint) -> Layout?
```

A layout for `size` bytes at `alignment`, or nothing when the pair cannot be one.
`size` and `alignment` are read by value; the layout is returned by copy. Reports `none` when `alignment` is
zero or not a power of two, and when rounding `size` up to `alignment` would pass the end of the address
space — which is the case that turns into an allocation far smaller than the caller asked for if it is not
caught here.
Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

| Name        | Type   | Description                                    |
| ----------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `size`      | `uint` | how many bytes are wanted                      |
| `alignment` | `uint` | the boundary the address must be a multiple of |

**Returns**: the layout, or `none` when `alignment` is not a usable power of two

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Layout.rux#L58)

<h3 id="for-bytes"><code>ForBytes</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ForBytes(size: uint) -> Layout?
```

A layout for `size` bytes at the alignment a machine word wants.
`size` is read by value. Reports `none` only when rounding `size` up would pass the end of the address space,
since the alignment is known good.
This is the layout for storage whose contents are bytes rather than a typed value: an allocation aligned to a
word suits anything the machine loads in one instruction.
Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

| Name   | Type   | Description               |
| ------ | ------ | ------------------------- |
| `size` | `uint` | how many bytes are wanted |

**Returns**: a layout of that size at its natural alignment, or `none` when there is none

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Layout.rux#L74)

## Methods

<h3 id="padded-size"><code>PaddedSize</code></h3>

```rux
pub func PaddedSize(self: &Layout) -> uint
```

The size this layout occupies once rounded up to its own alignment.
`self` is borrowed. This is the stride between two of these laid out one after another, and is what an arena
advances by. Cannot overflow, because [`New`](/docs/api/allocator/layout#new) refused every size for which it would.
Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the size rounded up to a whole number of alignments

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Layout.rux#L85)

<h3 id="is-satisfied-by"><code>IsSatisfiedBy</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsSatisfiedBy(self: &Layout, address: uint) -> bool
```

Whether `address` satisfies this layout's alignment.
`self` is borrowed and `address` is read by value and never dereferenced.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

| Name      | Type   | Description         |
| --------- | ------ | ------------------- |
| `address` | `uint` | the address to test |

**Returns**: whether `address` meets this layout's alignment

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Layout.rux#L97)

## Related

<h3 id="natural-alignment"><code>NaturalAlignment</code></h3>

```rux
pub func NaturalAlignment(size: uint) -> uint
```

The alignment a value of `size` bytes naturally wants.
`size` is read by value. Returns the largest power of two that divides a value of this size, capped at a machine
word, which is what every supported target's ABI requires of an ordinary value.
A size of zero reports one, since a zero-sized value has nothing to align.
Runs in time proportional to the word size and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Layout.rux#L127)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type   | Description                         |
| ------ | ------ | ----------------------------------- |
| `size` | `uint` | the size to choose an alignment for |

**Returns**: the largest useful power-of-two alignment for that size
